awayText.message: Purple blocks ads on Twitch live streams.

noChannel.message: Open a channel to turn Purple off or on there.

statusOff.message: Off on this channel: ads play

figureBreaksHint.message: Ad breaks Twitch started on this channel today: ads stitched into the stream and ads the page asks for

figureBlockedHint.message: Breaks Purple held back: no ad reached the player

figurePassedHint.message: Ads that reached the player and were shown

figureStallsHint.message: Times the video stopped by itself while playing: loading for half a second or more, or a frozen picture with sound

badgeHint.message: While Purple blocks an ad on a tab

exportHolds.message: The .txt holds the channel's last 7 days: ad breaks and how Purple handled them, stalls, audio and video sync, player errors and quality, the player version, whether Twitch marked your session ad-free, extensions touching the player, your browser and changed settings.

exportNot.message: It holds no Twitch account, password, token, cookie, IP address or video address.

exportPublic.message: The log stays on this computer: Purple never sends it. Anyone can read a file attached to a public GitHub issue, so check it before you attach it.

consent.message: I understand what the file holds

pickEmpty.message: No log yet. Purple keeps one for each channel you watch.

reportDownload.message: Download the log and open the report

exportSaved.message: The file is in your downloads. Open it and check it before you attach it to a bug report.

exportSavedReport.message: The file is in your downloads, and the bug report opened in a new tab: open the file, check it, then drag it into the report's "Purple log" field.

report.message: Open a bug report on GitHub

exportMissing.message: No channel was chosen. Open the export from the Purple popup.
